name: SHT31 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Sensirion digital temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.2 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±2 %) sensor with an I2C interface. Runs on 2.15–5.5 V. Sold as: SHT31-D breakout (6-pin: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, ADR, ALR), I2C address 0x44 (0x45 with ADR high).
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is, very accurately.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (pull-up fitted on most breakouts)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (pull-up fitted on most breakouts)

pins.name: ADR
pins.description: Address select: low or unconnected = 0x44, high = 0x45

pins.name: ALR
pins.description: Alert output (open-drain), not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: SHT31-D temperature humidity sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Single-shot command 0x24 0x00 then wait at least 15.5 ms before reading 6 bytes: temperature MSB, LSB, CRC, humidity MSB, LSB, CRC.
Check each CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
Leave ADR unconnected (pulled low on most boards) for address 0x44; tie it to VIN for 0x45, e.g. for a second sensor.
Keep the sensor away from the board's regulator and the ESP32, which warm the air around them.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sht31 import SHT31

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = SHT31(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
